recipes.title: BBQ Chicken Lollipops (Gas Grill)
recipes.cookTime: 20–25 min indirect + 8–10 min direct + 5 min rest

items.name: chicken drumsticks
items.gNote: 11 × 130 g raw (USDA drumstick, mid-point of 10–12); 33% bone removed (Canadian Nutrient File refuse); meat + skin record

items.name: lemon, zest only
items.gNote: zest of ½ lemon about 1 g

steps: French the drumsticks if you like (cut around the bone and push the meat down). Pat completely dry, then leave uncovered in the fridge 30–60 min.
Coat lightly with the marinade (no pooling). Marinate at least 1 h, ideally 3–6 h; overnight is fine.
Set up two zones: indirect low (~160–180°C) and direct medium-high (~200–220°C).
Indirect phase: lid closed, 20–25 min, turning every 5–7 min.
Crisping phase: move to direct heat for 8–10 min, turning every 1–2 min. If it flares up, move back to indirect briefly.
Warm the glaze ingredients so they stay thin. Brush on in the last 1–2 min only and flip once.
Check for 75°C internal, juices running clear. Rest 5 min.
tips: Lamb chop menu timing: start the chicken indirect → prep the lamb → crisp the chicken → rest it loosely covered → grill the lamb hot and fast → glaze both → serve.
Upgrades: a light smoke (wood chips on gas) or a touch of fresh lemon just before serving.

recipes.title: BBQ Chicken Wings (Kid-Friendly)
recipes.prepTime: 1 h brine + 30–60 min drying + 30–45 min rest
steps: Brine the wings in the fridge for 1 hour (no more than 2 hours).
Remove from the brine, rinse briefly and pat each wing completely dry. For the crispiest skin, leave them uncovered on a rack in the fridge 30–60 min.
Mix the rub thoroughly.
Massage the wings with the mayo and oil until only a very thin, glossy coat remains (no visible white mayo).
Add the rub in thirds, tossing and massaging after each addition.
Rest 30–45 min (cool room temperature if cooking soon, otherwise in the fridge).
Preheat the dome BBQ to 180–190°C. Cook over indirect heat 25–30 min, turning every 5–7 min.
Finish over direct heat for 8–10 min to crisp, until the thickest part reaches 85–90°C.
Warm the glaze ingredients until smooth. Brush on during the final 3–4 minutes, turning once or twice.
Rest 5 minutes. Finish with a light pinch of flaky sea salt.

extra.name: chicken wings (1.2 kg, from the yield)
extra.note: not in the ingredient list; 1.2 kg raw minus 46% bone (Canadian Nutrient File refuse for wings); meat + skin record

tips: A dry rub always tastes too salty off your finger. It's concentrated for 1.2 kg of meat.
Oven option: bake at 200°C for 35–45 min on a wire rack over a tray.
Don't overcrowd the grill, and never glaze early (the sugar burns).

recipes.title: BBQ Pulled Chicken (Pressure Cooker)
recipes.cookTime: 7 min high pressure + 5 min natural release + 4–6 min sauté

items.name: olive oil
items.note: only if sautéing the onion first

items.name: brown sugar
items.note: only if the sauce isn't already sweet

items.name: water or chicken stock
items.note: in the pot first (120 ml if burn-prone)

items.name: Dijon mustard
items.gNote: no Dijon record; prepared mustard used

steps: Mix the BBQ sauce, Worcestershire, vinegar, paste, spices, sugar, and the grated onion and garlic in a bowl. (Or sauté the onion in oil 2–3 min and the garlic 20–30 sec first.)
Pour the water/stock into the pressure cooker first, add the chicken in a single layer, then pour the sauce over. Don't stir it into the base (avoids a burn warning).
High pressure 7 min (8 max for very thick breasts).
Leave it untouched 5 min, then carefully open the manual valve to release the rest (keep hands and face away).
Check the thickest part is cooked, then shred with two forks and return to the pot.
Sauté 4–6 min, stirring gently, until the sauce thickens, clings and the raw onion taste is gone. Don't over-reduce; breast tightens.
Adjust: 1–2 tbsp more BBQ sauce for richness, 1 tsp vinegar if too sweet, black pepper.
Slaw: mix everything and rest 10–15 min.
tips: With thighs (best): 1.2–1.5 kg, 1½ cups BBQ sauce, 60–80 ml liquid, 10 min high pressure (11–12 for large), 5 min rest, then 5–8 min reduction.
Serve on toasted buns with slaw and pickles, in wraps, or over baked potatoes.

recipes.title: Brined BBQ Chicken Drumsticks
recipes.prepTime: 2–4 h brine + 1–4 h drying + 30–45 min rest
steps: Brine the drumsticks in the fridge 2–4 hours (no more than about 6 hours).
Remove from the brine. Don't rinse; pat them extremely dry.
Ideally refrigerate them uncovered for 1–4 hours to dry the skin (even 30–60 min helps).
Coat thinly with the mayo and oil, then add the rub in thirds, massaging well. Rest 30–45 min.
Cook indirectly at 180–190°C for 35–45 min, turning every 8–10 min.
Finish over direct heat 5–10 min, turning often to crisp the skin.
Warm the glaze and brush it on only during the final 3–5 min.
Aim for 82–88°C internal near the thickest part, not touching the bone (about 85°C is ideal). Rest 5–10 minutes.

extra.name: chicken drumsticks (1.2 kg, from the yield)
extra.note: not in the ingredient list; 1.2 kg raw minus 33% bone (Canadian Nutrient File refuse for drumsticks); meat + skin record

recipes.title: Chicken Shawarma (Oven, Lebanese-Style)
recipes.prepTime: 4 h minimum marinating (ideal 8–16 h, max ~24 h)

items.name: neutral oil
items.gNote: marinade counted in full (some drips off, so this errs high)

items.name: seven spice
items.gNote: no seven-spice record; allspice (the listed swap) used

items.name: olive oil
items.note: or a small knob of butter

items.name: pita or flatbread
items.gNote: assumed 1 large pita (60 g) a serving

items.name: tomato paste or red pepper paste

steps: Mix the marinade, coat the chicken well, cover and refrigerate at least 4 h (ideally 8–16 h; not over ~24 h).
Mix the sauce and rest it 10–15 min. Toss the pickle veg with vinegar, salt and sugar and leave 15–30 min.
Preheat the oven to 220°C (fan if possible). Use a rack over a tray for airflow.
Lift the chicken out, letting excess marinade drip off (don't pour it on the tray). Spread in a single layer with no overlap.
Roast 20 min.
Flip and roast 10–15 min more, until lightly browned with slightly dry edges.
Switch to grill/broiler on high for 3–6 min, watching closely, until the edges char.
Immediately toss with 1 tsp olive oil or butter, plus a squeeze of lemon if you like.
Build: warm pita, sauce, chicken, pickles, and fries if using.
Optional: brush the wrap with the oil, paste and pomegranate molasses mix and toast in a pan until golden.
tips: Overcrowding is the #1 failure: it steams instead of browning.
Keep the acid moderate in the marinade (vinegar + zest only). Lemon juice goes on at the end.

recipes.title: KFC-Style Chicken Fillets (Air Fryer)
recipes.prepTime: 1 h minimum marinating (3–4 h better) + 10 min rest after coating

items.name: buttermilk
items.gNote: whole buttermilk; counted in full though much stays in the bowl (errs high)

items.name: flour
items.gNote: coating counted in full though some is left over (errs high)

steps: Slice whole breasts horizontally into even, thinner fillets; flatten any thick parts.
Mix the buttermilk, egg, salt, pepper and paprika. Add the chicken, cover and marinate at least 1 h (3–4 h better).
Mix the coating. Drizzle in 2–3 tbsp of marinade and rub with your fingertips to create craggy clumps.
Let excess marinade drip off each piece and press firmly into the flour. For a thicker crust, dip back in the marinade and flour again.
Rest the coated pieces on a tray for 10 min.
Preheat the air fryer to 190°C. Spray both sides well with oil.
Single layer: cook 8 min, turn, spray again if needed, then 6–10 min more until golden and 74°C inside.
Rest on a rack 3–5 min; don't stack.
tips: Floury, pale coating = not enough oil spray. Spray more and continue.
For burgers: make the fillets flatter and cook about 14–16 min total. Serve with a soft bun, mayo/pepper mayo, lettuce, cheese and pickles.
Goes with KFC-style gravy and mash (see those recipes).

recipes.title: Sweet & Sour Chicken (Takeaway-Style)

items.name: baking soda
items.nc: velveting; no calories, protein, carbs or fat, and its sodium isn't tracked here

items.name: water
items.nc: velveting; no calories, protein, carbs or fat

items.name: rice vinegar
items.gNote: no rice-vinegar record; distilled vinegar used

items.name: pineapple chunks
items.gNote: fresh; canned in juice is similar

items.name: oil for deep-frying
items.gNote: oil absorbed while deep-frying: 15% of the raw weight going into the oil, assumed (typical uptake for battered/dough foods; Grasas y Aceites 1998, doi:10.3989/gya.1998.v49.i3-4.729); chicken + flour + starch ≈ 900 g

items.name: potato starch
items.gNote: no potato-starch record; cornstarch used (same energy)

steps: Velvet: mix the chicken, baking soda and water. Rest 15–20 min, rinse thoroughly and pat completely dry.
Add all the marinade ingredients, mix well and rest 15 min. It should feel slightly sticky, not wet.
Whisk the batter just before frying. Keep it cold and don't overmix; slight lumps are fine.
First fry: dip the chicken in the batter and fry at 170°C for 3–4 min until pale and set. Rest 2–3 min.
Second fry: 190°C until deep golden and crisp.
Sauce: simmer everything except the slurry, then stir in the slurry slowly and cook until glossy and coating the back of a spoon.
Wok toss on high heat: onion and peppers 1–2 min max, add the pineapple and sauce, toss in the chicken quickly (under 2 min) and serve immediately.
tips: Cornstarch for the batter/marinade, potato starch for the sauce slurry (glossy, silky). If you only have one, cornstarch works for both.
"Tomato sauce" here means ketchup. If using plain tomato sauce, add 1 extra tbsp sugar + 1 tsp vinegar per 6 tbsp.
Too tangy? Add 1–2 tsp sugar or a splash of pineapple juice. Coat lightly and don't let it sit in the sauce.

recipes.title: Beef Mince Tacos

items.name: lean beef mince
items.gNote: 85% lean raw record (the fattier end of 10–15%)

items.name: olive oil
items.note: only if using very lean mince

items.name: flour or corn tortillas
items.gNote: 9 × 30 g small flour tortillas (mid-point of 8–10; flour, the higher-calorie option)

items.name: mature cheddar or Monterey Jack
items.gNote: no amount; 15 g a serving assumed

items.name: avocado or guacamole
items.gNote: no amount; ½ avocado for the table assumed

items.name: fresh coriander, lime wedges, hot sauce
chipotle in adobo
items.note: finely minced (or 1 tsp adobo sauce for mild)
items.gNote: no chipotle-in-adobo record; chili powder used

steps: Make the lime sauce (mix and chill). Mix the salsa and let it stand 10 min. Mix the pickled onions and leave at least 20 min.
Heat a large pan over high heat. Add the mince and let it brown well before breaking it up; cook until the moisture evaporates and it caramelises.
Reduce to medium. Add the onion for about 5 min until soft, then the garlic for 1 min.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2–3 min until it darkens. Add all the spices (and chipotle/cocoa if using) and cook 30–60 seconds.
Add the stock, Worcestershire and sugar. Simmer gently 8–10 min until the liquid coats the meat.
Finish with the lime juice and adjust the seasoning.
Warm the tortillas over a gas flame 15–20 seconds per side (or in a dry pan) and wrap them in a towel.
Assemble: beef, cheese, lettuce, salsa, avocado, pickled onions, lime sauce, coriander and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Use freshly grated cheese; it melts better than pre-shredded.
Don't overcook the mince after the stock goes in. Add a splash more stock if it gets dry.
Stir 1 tsp butter into the beef just before serving for extra richness. It tastes even better the next day.
For 500 g mince, set the scaler to ⅔× (about 6–8 tacos).

recipes.title: Pepper Steak Pie (Pressure Cooker)
recipes.cookTime: Pressure cook 35 min + 10–15 min release + 10–20 min reduce; bake 15 min blind + 25–30 min

items.name: chuck steak or stewing beef
items.gNote: chuck arm pot roast, lean and fat, raw (a fattier record than trimmed stew meat, so fat errs high)

items.name: English or Dijon mustard
items.gNote: no English/Dijon record; prepared mustard used

items.name: beer
items.gNote: counted in full; some alcohol cooks off (errs high)

items.name: cornflour
items.note: only if needed, with 2 tbsp cold water

items.name: shortcrust pastry
items.gNote: 1 sheet = 400 g assumed (common roll size); pie-crust record

items.name: puff pastry
items.gNote: 1 sheet = 400 g assumed (common roll size); trimmings counted

items.name: egg, beaten
items.gNote: egg wash: about half the egg is used

steps: Pat the beef very dry. Mix the flour with 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper, toss the beef through it and shake off the excess.
Brown the beef in batches on sauté (or in a separate pan) until deeply coloured. Set aside.
Cook the onion and carrot 4–5 min, add the mushrooms 4–5 min until their water cooks off, then the garlic 1 min and the tomato paste 1–2 min.
Add the mustard, Worcestershire and soy and scrape the bottom well (avoids a burn warning).
Add the beef, stock, beer, thyme, bay leaf, sugar, ½ tsp salt and 1–2 tsp pepper.
Seal and cook on high pressure 35 min. Natural release 10–15 min, then release the rest. If the beef is still firm, cook another 8–10 min.
Remove the bay leaf and thyme stems. Sauté uncovered 10–20 min until thick and glossy; it must coat the beef, not run. If still thin, stir in the cornflour slurry for 2–3 min.
Stir in the butter and extra cracked pepper (1–2 tsp), and adjust the salt.
Cool the filling 45–60 min, until lukewarm or cold (spread it on a tray to speed up).
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Line a pie dish with shortcrust and prick it. Blind bake with paper and weights 10 min, then uncovered 5 min.
Fill with the cooled filling, brush the edge with egg, cover with puff pastry, crimp, trim and cut 2–3 slits. Egg wash the top.
Bake at 200°C for 25–30 min until deeply golden and risen. Rest 10 min.
tips: Stovetop instead: cover and simmer 1½–2 h until tender, then uncovered 15–25 min to thicken.
Use freshly cracked pepper, not fine powder (it tastes dusty and harsh). Keep the tomato to 1 tbsp paste.
Shortcrust bottom + puff top. Puff on the bottom goes soft.
Serve with creamy mash, peas and a little tomato sauce or chutney.

recipes.title: Pork Ribs: Spritz, Wrap & Glaze (Gas Grill)
recipes.cookTime: Wrapped 1–1.5 h (baby back) or 1.5–2 h (spare/St Louis) at 120–135°C + about 10 min + 10–15 min glazing

items.name: apple juice
items.note: or 2 tsp apple juice and 1 tsp cider vinegar

items.name: barbecue sauce
items.note: sweet-tangy tomato style, not very smoky
items.gNote: generic barbecue sauce record; all of it counted

steps: Unwrapped smoke phase: leave them alone. No basting. At most a light spritz every 45–60 min, only once the bark has started to set.
Wrap when the bark feels tacky-dry and set, the colour is deep mahogany and it smells smoky (yours needed about 20–40 min more from the photo stage).
Lay out foil, add the butter, honey and splash of apple juice/vinegar, place the ribs meat side down (bone side up) and wrap tightly. No BBQ sauce in the wrap.
Cook wrapped at 120–135°C: baby back 1–1.5 h, spare/St Louis 1.5–2 h. Start checking at about 1 h 15 min.
Done when the rack bends easily, the bones pull back and a probe slides between the bones with little resistance.
Unwrap carefully (hot juices), put back on the grill unwrapped and let the surface tighten about 10 min.
Brush on a thin layer of glaze, cook 5–7 min, then an optional second thin layer for 5–7 min. 1–2 light coats is enough.

nutrition.basis: wrap and glaze only; the ribs and rub aren't listed, so they aren't counted

tips: Homemade glaze: 120 ml ketchup, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp cider vinegar, 1 tsp Worcestershire, ½ tsp smoked paprika, ¼ tsp garlic powder, black pepper, plus 1–2 tsp water. Warm until smooth.
Sharper glaze: 4 tbsp BBQ sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 2 tsp cider vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tsp Worcestershire.

recipes.title: Shredded Beef Melts with Dipping Broth
recipes.cookTime: Oven 3.5–4.5 h at 150–160°C, stovetop 3–4 h, or slow cooker 7–8 h low / 5–6 h high; broth reduction 10–20 min

items.name: chuck roast
items.gNote: chuck arm pot roast, lean and fat, raw (a fattier record than trimmed stew meat, so fat errs high)

items.name: good beef stock
items.gNote: broth counted in full, including the dip (errs high)

items.name: sturdy bread
items.gNote: 14 slices × 45 g assumed (mid-point of 12–16, paired with 7 sandwiches); french/sourdough record

items.name: softened butter
items.gNote: no amount; 5 g a slice assumed

steps: Blend the stock, vinegar, tomatoes, onion, garlic, cumin, chilli, oregano and cloves until smooth. Keep the bay leaves aside.
Pat the beef dry and season generously. Sear in batches in oil over medium-high until well browned. Return all the beef to the pot.
Pour in the blended liquid (at least halfway up the meat) and add the bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer and cover.
Braise until a fork pulls it apart with almost no resistance: oven 150–160°C 3.5–4.5 h, very low stovetop 3–4 h, or slow cooker 7–8 h low / 5–6 h high.
Lift out the beef and discard the bay. Strain the liquid into a saucepan and skim some fat.
Simmer the broth 10–20 min to concentrate. Balance with 1 tsp sugar/honey if sharp, then salt and pepper.
Shred the beef with two forks and moisten with a few spoonfuls of broth (not soaked).
Butter one side of each slice. On the unbuttered side: cheese, beef, more cheese (and coriander), then top with a buttered-side-out slice.
Toast in a skillet over medium heat until deep golden and melted through.
Serve immediately with bowls of hot dipping broth.
tips: Cook to tenderness, not a temperature: 200°F internal doesn't guarantee it's shreddable.
Use sturdy bread that holds up to dipping. Don't over-shred into mush.

recipes.title: Slow-Roasted Spiced Lamb (1.7 kg)
recipes.prepTime: 1 h minimum marinating (overnight better) + 45–60 min out of the fridge
recipes.cookTime: 3–4½ h covered at 160°C (150°C fan) + 20–30 min uncovered at 220°C + 15–20 min rest

items.name: deboned lamb shoulder or leg
items.note: rolled and tied if opened out
items.gNote: shoulder, lean and fat, raw (leg is leaner)

items.name: garlic
items.note: halved across, or 6 extra cloves smashed

steps: Pat the lamb very dry. If it's opened out or uneven, roll loosely and tie into a roast shape.
Mix all the rub ingredients into a thick paste and rub all over, into every fold.
Marinate at least 1 h, better overnight in the fridge. Take out 45–60 min before cooking.
Heat the oven to 160°C conventional / 150°C fan. Spread the onions, garlic and bay in a roasting dish, add the stock and sit the lamb on top.
Cover very tightly with foil (double layer) or a lid.
Roast covered: shoulder 3.5–4.5 h, leg 3–4 h. Start checking near the lower end. It's ready when a skewer slides in with almost no resistance and it's close to pull-apart.
Uncover, adding a splash of water if the pan is dry. Brush with the honey, molasses and pan juice mix.
Raise to 220°C conventional / 210°C fan and roast uncovered 20–30 min until dark, glossy and caramelised.
Rest 15–20 min. Slice thickly or pull into chunks and spoon over the pan juices.
tips: Why it was tough last time: it was pulled at a "done" temperature. For this style, tenderness is the endpoint, not internal temperature.
Leg is leaner: keep it at 150–160°C, make sure there's liquid in the pan, check earlier, and stop once it's soft.
Serve with Kabsa-Style Rice, saffron/vermicelli rice, roast potatoes, flatbreads or cucumber-mint yoghurt.

recipes.title: Sticky Lamb Chops (Gas Grill)
recipes.cookTime: 7–10 min on the grill + 5 min rest

items.name: lamb chops
items.gNote: 10 chops × 85 g edible (mid-point of 8–12; about 115 g each with bone, ~25% bone assumed); loin chop record

items.name: lemon
items.gNote: juice of 1 lemon (48 g) + zest counted with it

items.name: Dijon mustard
items.gNote: no Dijon record; prepared mustard used

steps: Pat the chops completely dry. Mix the marinade and coat the chops evenly by hand.
Marinate at least 30 min, ideally 2–4 h, and no longer than overnight. Take out of the fridge 20–30 min before cooking.
Simmer the glaze ingredients gently for 2–3 min until slightly thickened, glossy and still brushable. Set aside.
Preheat the grill to medium-high (230–260°C) with a slightly cooler backup zone. Clean and lightly oil the grates.
Direct heat: 4–5 min on the first side, flip once, 3–5 min on the second. Move to the cooler zone briefly if it flares up.
When about 5°C below target, brush glaze on one side, flip, brush again: 60–90 sec total.
Target 57°C for medium-rare or 63°C for medium. Remove slightly early.
Rest at least 5 min, loosely tented with foil.
tips: Very fatty chops: extra lemon zest. Thick chops (>3 cm): finish on indirect heat before glazing.
More tender: add 1 tbsp Greek yoghurt to the marinade. For kids: slightly less garlic.
Pair with something fresh and acidic (tomato-cucumber salad, herb rice). Avoid heavy creamy sides.

recipes.title: Sticky Pork Belly (Braise, Fry & Glaze)
recipes.cookTime: Braise 2–2½ h (+20–30 min if needed) + brown and glaze about 30 min

items.name: pork belly
items.gNote: raw, all fat counted though some renders out (errs high)

steps: Place the belly skin-side down and slice off the rind in one piece (keep it for crackling). Cut the meat into 4–5 cm chunks.
Put the pork in a heavy pot with the stock, garlic, ginger, sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper. Bring just to the boil, then immediately turn down to a very gentle simmer, lid ajar.
Cook 2–2½ h until tender when pierced: soft all the way through, holding its shape, not stringy.
Lift the pork out onto paper towel, pat very dry and leave uncovered 15–20 min.
Mix the glaze with 2 tbsp soy, taste, and add the third only if needed. It should taste sweet first, savoury second.
Brown the pork in batches in a little oil over medium-high, 2–3 min per side, without overcrowding.
Return all the pork, lower to medium, add the glaze and cook 4–7 min, turning gently, until sticky and glossy. Add a splash of water if it tightens too fast.
Finish with spring onions and sesame seeds. Serve with light coconut rice and something fresh.
tips: What happened on the day: at 2 h the fat was soft but the meat strands were still firm, so it needed another 20–30 min. Don't glaze until it's soft all the way through.
Crackling: pat the rind dry, rub with oil and plenty of salt, and roast at 220°C for 25–40 min until puffed.
Pressure cooker alternative: 35–40 min, then 10 min release, then dry, fry and glaze the same way.
Kid-simple glaze: leave out the sesame oil and paprika.

recipes.title: Beef Curry (Pressure Cooker + Slow Cooker)
recipes.cookTime: Pressure cook 12–15 min + slow cook 3–4 h LOW

items.name: ginger-garlic paste
items.gNote: ginger-garlic paste: garlic record; 1½ tbsp about 22 g

items.name: Kashmiri chilli powder
items.gNote: Kashmiri chilli is pure ground chilli: cayenne record

items.name: garam masala
items.gNote: no garam-masala record; cumin (a main component) used

items.name: tamarind paste
items.note: or ½–1 tsp vinegar; start small

steps: Pressure cook the beef to 70–80% tender (not fully): beef, turmeric, salt and water. Stovetop: 2 whistles on medium then natural release; electric: 12–15 min high pressure, natural release. Keep beef and all the stock.
Heat oil in a wide pan. Add 1 sprig curry leaves and green chillies (optional). Add onions and shallots and cook until deep golden brown, 12–18 min.
Add ginger-garlic paste; cook 2–3 min.
Add the tomato paste and fry 2–3 min until it darkens and smells sweet (if using fresh tomato, cook it down until jammy, 6–8 min).

Lower the heat. Add both chilli powders, coriander, fennel, optional warm spices and fenugreek, ½ tsp of the black pepper and 1 tsp of the garam masala. Add 3–5 tbsp beef stock to make a paste and cook 2 min, stirring.
Add the beef and toss to coat. Add all remaining stock and simmer 5 min.
Transfer to the slow cooker and cook LOW 3–4 hours (or LOW 3 h then WARM until dinner). Don't add extra water early; if it gets too thick later add 50–100 ml hot water.

Finish: pour into a pot and boil 8–12 min until thicker and glossy. Add the remaining 1 tsp garam masala, remaining ½–1 tsp pepper, tamarind (or vinegar) gradually, optional ghee and the last curry-leaf sprig for 2 min.
Rest 15–30 min if you can. Serve with rice, naan, roti or paratha.
tips: No-tomato version: skip the tomato paste and use tamarind paste 1–2 tsp (or vinegar 1–1½ tsp) to balance.
If you add potatoes in the slow cooker they soften long before the beef: take them out and return them for the last 20–30 min.
Chewy beef with time running out: add 120 ml hot water/stock, switch to HIGH for 45–60 min and don't lift the lid; or pressure cook the beef + gravy (no potatoes) 10–12 min electric / 2–3 whistles.

Heat the butter and oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions with a pinch of salt 8–10 min until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, curry powder, cumin, cinnamon, nutmeg and smoked paprika; cook about 1 min without burning.
Deglaze with about 60 ml of the stock, scraping the bottom of the pot.

steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb well, 6–8 min. Season with 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper.
Add onion and celery stems (and carrots, if using). Cook 6–8 min until softened.
Add garlic, cilantro stems and parsley stems. Cook 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste, ginger, turmeric, cumin, cinnamon and paprika. Fry 60–90 seconds to bloom the spices.
Add crushed tomatoes, saffron infusion and the 1.3 L broth. Scrape up the browned bits and bring to a gentle simmer for 5–10 min.

Option A (canned chickpeas): add lentils, simmer gently 25–30 min until about 90% tender; add chickpeas and simmer 10–15 min more. Option B (soaked chickpeas): add chickpeas and simmer 40–50 min (top up with hot water); add lentils and simmer 25–30 min more. Pressure cooker for B: add chickpeas and lentils, 20 min High, quick release.

Whisk the flour and cold water until completely smooth. Stir the soup and pour the slurry in slowly in a thin stream. Simmer 8–10 min, stirring often, until thickened and the flour taste is gone. For a lighter soup start with 2 tbsp flour.

Stir in most of the cilantro and parsley leaves (and the celery leaves, if you like). Taste for salt and pepper, and loosen with hot water/broth to "hearty but spoonable".
Optional egg: turn the heat off, wait 60–90 seconds, then drizzle in the beaten egg while stirring continuously (don't boil afterwards). Optional: stir in 1 tbsp smen/butter.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and the reserved herbs.
tips: Harira thickens as it sits. Reheat with a splash of water/broth and re-check the seasoning.
Add lemon to the bowls, not the pot, unless you're serving it all at once.
The flavour improves overnight; add fresh herbs when you serve.

Kid-friendly version: after the tomatoes and stock go in (only 1 L stock at that stage), simmer in the ginger 5–10 min, then blend the whole vegetable/tomato base smooth. Add 250–300 ml more stock, then the lentils (25–30 min), chickpeas (10–15 min) and vermicelli (6–10 min). Stir in separately cooked lamb at the end.

Separately cooked lamb: season a thick lamb leg steak and cook covered with foil at 160°C on onions with a little water for up to about 2 h, until a knife goes in easily. Rest 10 min, cut into bite-size pieces, sear 1–2 min in a very hot pan, then deglaze with a little soup and add the strained cooking juices to the soup.
When the base is blended, you may need no tadouira at all, or only 1 tbsp flour with about 60 ml water. Judge it after the legumes have cooked.

steps: Pre-ferment: dissolve the yeast in the water, mix into the flour to a loose wet dough (no kneading). Cover 2–3 h until doubled and yeasty-smelling.

items.note: with a tiny pinch salt, pinch sugar, oregano, drizzle of oil

items.name: cheese
items.note: mozzarella or a mozzarella/mild cheddar mix

items.name: kid-friendly toppings
items.note: ham, sweetcorn, pineapple, chicken, mild pepperoni, thin mushrooms

steps: Mix the water, yeast and sugar/honey. Add the flour, salt and oil and mix to a rough dough.
Knead 6–8 min by hand or 4–5 min in a mixer until smooth, soft and not sticky. If it's sticky, rest it 10 min before adding flour.
Cover and leave at room temperature 60–90 min until slightly puffed.
Refrigerate 24–48 hours (72 h max).
Take it out 45–60 min before rolling. Divide into balls: 32–35 g for thin bases, 38–40 g recommended for kids, 40–45 g for softer, thicker bases.
Rest the balls 15–20 min, then roll into 10 cm rounds about 2–3 mm thick.
Preheat the oven to 240–250°C with an upside-down tray, stone or steel inside for 20–30 min.
Par-bake each base 2–3 min until set, pale and slightly puffed, not browned. Press down any big puffs.
Cool completely on a rack, stack with baking paper between them, wrap tightly and refrigerate (best within 2 days, or freeze).
Party day: preheat to 220–240°C. Top lightly and bake 5–7 min until the cheese melts and the edges are lightly golden.

nutrition.basis: dough, sauce and cheese; extra toppings aren't counted

tips: Don't par-bake for only seconds or a minute; the bases stay doughy after refrigeration.
Avoid wet toppings like thick tomato slices; mini bases go soggy.
Best plan: make the dough → cold ferment → par-bake the day before → refrigerate → top and bake on the day.

recipes.title: NY-Style Pizza Dough (Same-Day, 4-Hour)

servings.text: 4 large pizzas (300 g balls) or 5 medium (240–250 g)

recipes.prepTime: About 4 h total (mix, knead, 1½–2 h bulk, 1½–2 h ball proof)

items.name: Manitoba "0" flour
items.gNote: no Manitoba record; bread flour used

items.name: cold or cool water
items.note: up to 480–500 g total with Manitoba 0, added 10 g at a time

items.name: instant dry yeast
items.gNote: instant yeast: active dry record used

steps: Mix the flour, semolina, 460 g water, sugar and yeast until no dry flour remains. Cover and rest 15–20 min (20 min for Manitoba flour).
Check the texture. If it's still dry or tears, add water 10 g at a time (usually about 20 g extra for Manitoba 0).
Add the salt and olive oil (oil gradually if mixing by hand). Knead 8–10 min by hand or 5–7 min in a mixer until smooth, elastic and slightly tacky.
Bulk rise covered at room temperature (ideally 24–27°C) for 1½–2 hours, until slightly risen and relaxed; it doesn't need to double. Check after 75–90 min in a warm kitchen.
Divide into 4 × 300 g or 5 × 240–250 g and shape tight balls. Place in lightly oiled covered containers or on a tray.
Ball proof 1½–2 hours until puffy, relaxed and stretchable without springing back.
Meanwhile preheat the oven as hot as possible (250–300°C) with a steel or stone for 45–60 min.
Stretch the dough by hand (no rolling pin), top lightly with sauce, cheese and toppings, and bake 6–9 min until the base is firm, the rim browned and the slice folds without cracking.

extra.name: oil for the dough containers
extra.note: step 5; amount not given, 2 tsp assumed

tips: Schedule: 0:00 mix → 0:15 salt + oil, knead → 0:30–2:15 bulk → 2:15 ball → 2:15–4:00 proof → 4:00 bake.
Max proofing temperature is about 28–30°C. Don't proof outside at 35°C; it overproofs fast. An oven with only the light on works if it stays under 30°C.
Manitoba 0 beats 00 here: stronger, chewier and easier to stretch.

Cold-ferment (poolish) version for more flavour: poolish of 250 g flour + 250 g water + 0.5–1 g yeast + 5 g honey, left 12–16 h. Final dough: poolish + 500 g flour + 50 g semolina + 200–225 g cold water + 1 g yeast, rest 15–20 min, then 22 g salt + 30 g oil. Knead, rest 45–60 min, ball, refrigerate 24–48 h, and take out 2–3 h before baking.

recipes.title: Skillet Cornbread

items.name: buttermilk
items.note: or milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice/vinegar, stood 5 min

items.name: unsalted butter
items.note: melted and slightly cooled, plus a knob for the skillet

items.name: softened butter
items.gNote: honey butter, served on the side

steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C with a 23 cm cast-iron skillet inside.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, bicarb and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl whisk the eggs, buttermilk, milk and melted butter.
Pour the wet into the dry and mix until just combined; don't overmix. (With medium cornmeal, let the batter sit 10–15 min.)
Carefully take out the hot skillet, add a small knob of butter and swirl to coat.
Pour in the batter immediately and bake 20–25 min until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm with honey butter.
tips: Medium cornmeal works; don't grind it. Rest the batter 10–15 min and add 15–30 ml extra milk if it's thick. If it's polenta-coarse, pulse it briefly or soak it in the buttermilk for 20–30 min.
Sweetcorn: skip it when serving with braai meat or stew (better texture, slices cleanly). Add a drained can for a moister family-style bread.
For extra moisture, replace 60 ml of the milk with sour cream or Greek yogurt.

recipes.title: Skillet Naan (Soft & Stretchy)
recipes.prepTime: 15 min autolyse + 8–10 min knead + 1–1½ h rise + 20–30 min rest

items.name: warm water
items.note: 38–40°C, plus up to 60 ml extra only if needed

items.name: active dry yeast
items.note: about 2¼ tsp (or the same amount of instant yeast, mixed into the flour)

steps: Activate the yeast: stir the sugar into 240 ml warm water (38–40°C), sprinkle over the yeast and leave 5–10 min until foamy.
Mix the flour, salt, baking soda and baking powder. Add the yeast mixture, yogurt and melted butter and mix to a rough dough.
Autolyse: rest 15 minutes before kneading.
Knead 8–10 min by hand (5–6 in a mixer) until very soft, slightly tacky, smooth and elastic. If firm, add extra water 1 tbsp at a time.
First rise: 1–1½ hours until doubled (or refrigerate overnight for deeper flavour).
Divide into 10 balls (about 85–90 g each). Rest 20–30 min covered.
Roll to 3 mm thick or stretch by hand. Press garlic/seeds onto one side if using.
Heat cast iron until almost smoking. Cook naan in the dry pan 60–90 seconds until big bubbles form, flip and cook 60–90 seconds.
Brush immediately with butter or ghee.

extra.name: butter for brushing
extra.note: step 9; amount not given, 1 tsp a naan assumed

tips: For extra puff, press the cooked naan briefly over an open flame (10–15 sec), or press the edges down with a spatula.
Fridge: refrigerate the dough after kneading (or after the first rise) for up to 48 h. Bring it to room temperature for 60 min, then divide and cook.
Don't overcrowd the pan. Slightly wetter dough gives softer naan.

recipes.title: Soetbrood (South African Sweet Bread)
recipes.prepTime: 10–12 min knead + 1–1½ h rise + 45–60 min proof

items.name: mixed spice
items.gNote: no mixed-spice record; pumpkin pie spice (a similar blend) used

steps: Mix the flour, salt, sugar, yeast and spices. Stir in the raisins.
Whisk the water, melted butter and egg together. Add to the dry ingredients and mix into a soft dough.
Knead 10–12 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover in a greased bowl and rise until doubled, about 1–1½ hours.
Shape into 2 large loaves or 1 large round loaf. Proof again 45–60 minutes.
Bake at 180°C for 35–45 minutes until golden brown.
While still hot, brush with the warm apricot jam glaze.
tips: Variations: 50–100 g mixed peel, extra cinnamon, chopped almonds, orange zest.
Excellent toasted the next day with salted butter.

Lighter single loaf: 500 g bread flour, 7 g instant yeast, 75 g sugar, 5 g salt, 1 tsp cinnamon, ¼ tsp nutmeg, 250 ml lukewarm milk, 1 egg, 60 g butter, 150 g raisins, orange zest. Rise 1–1½ h, then proof in a 23 × 13 cm tin 45–60 min. Egg wash and bake at 180°C for 30–35 min (93–95°C inside).

recipes.title: Vetkoek (Tuckshop-Style)
recipes.prepTime: Knead 8–10 min + 60–90 min rise + 20–30 min second rise

items.name: oil for deep-frying
items.gNote: oil absorbed while deep-frying: 15% of the raw weight going into the oil, assumed (typical uptake for battered/dough foods; Grasas y Aceites 1998, doi:10.3989/gya.1998.v49.i3-4.729); dough ≈ 900 g; sunflower record

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a big bowl.
Add 300 ml lukewarm water and the oil. Mix, then knead 8–10 min until smooth, elastic, soft and slightly tacky. Add a little water if stiff.
Cover and rise somewhere warm until doubled, about 60–90 min.
Punch down gently and divide into 10–12 pieces (75–90 g). Shape smooth balls and flatten into thick discs.
Second rise: on a lightly oiled tray, covered, 20–30 min until puffy.
Heat oil to 170–180°C (a test bit should bubble and rise in about 5 sec).
Fry 2–3 at a time, 2–3 min per side until deep golden, turning once or twice. Drain on paper towel.
tips: Greasy vetkoek = oil too cool. Don't crowd the pot; don't skip the second rise; keep the dough soft.
Fillings: mince curry, syrup + butter or jam, cheese + polony, chicken mayo, apricot jam + cheddar.

recipes.title: Coconut Jasmine Rice (Light)

items.name: jasmine rice
items.gNote: 2 cups × 185 g; no jasmine record, long-grain white used

items.name: water
items.note: 1½ cups if using ¾ cup coconut milk

steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear.
Put the rice, coconut milk, water, salt, sugar (and ginger/pandan) in a pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring once only.
Cover tightly, reduce to very low and cook 12–15 min.
Turn off the heat and rest covered 10 min. Remove the ginger/pandan and fluff with a fork.
tips: Rice cooker: same ingredients, stir once, use the normal white rice setting, then 10 min on warm.
Keep it lightly coconutty, not dessert-style. Skip mango with pork belly; add cucumber, greens or a lime wedge instead.

recipes.title: Creamy Mashed Potatoes
steps: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold, well-salted water.
Bring to a gentle boil and cook 15–20 min until a knife slides in easily.
Drain, return to the hot pot on very low heat for 1–2 min to dry out.
Mash or rice. Don't use a blender/food processor (it goes gluey).
Mix in the butter first, then gradually add the warm cream and milk until soft and creamy.
Season and adjust.
tips: Everyday ratio per 1 kg: 100 g butter + 150 ml warm milk (or 100–120 g butter with 120–180 ml milk/cream).
Flavour add-ins: 2–3 tbsp cream cheese, 2 tbsp sour cream, 1–2 roasted garlic cloves, a pinch of nutmeg, chives.
Great with KFC-Style Gravy.

recipes.title: Kabsa-Style Rice
recipes.cookTime: About 15 min + 10 min rest (after building the base)
steps: Wash the rice until the water runs mostly clear, soak 20–30 min and drain.
Heat the oil/ghee and cook the onion 8–10 min until golden. Add the garlic for 30 sec.
Add the tomatoes, paste and carrot and cook 5–7 min until thick and fragrant.
Add all the whole and ground spices, bay leaf and chillies, and cook 1 min to bloom.
Add the rice and stir gently 1 min. Pour in 3 cups hot stock and season; the liquid should taste slightly too salty. Add the raisins now if using.
Bring to a gentle boil, cover tightly on minimum heat 15 min, then off the heat covered 10 min. Fluff.
If it's slightly underdone, add a splash of hot stock, cover and steam 5 min more.
Serve on a platter topped with the lamb, pan juices, toasted nuts and coriander.

recipes.title: Mexican Corn Ribs (Tajín & Lemon)
recipes.cookTime: Grill 8–10 min / air fryer 12–15 min at 200°C / oven 20–25 min at 220°C fan

items.name: smoked paprika
items.note: or regular paprika if you have none

items.name: Tajín (chilli-lime)
items.gNote: no Tajín record; chili powder used (Tajín is mostly salt and chilli, so this errs high)

steps: Trim the ends flat, stand each cob upright and cut in half lengthwise, then halve again into rib strips. Use a heavy knife and firm downward pressure. If too hard, microwave the whole cob 2–3 min first.
Toss the ribs with melted butter, paprika, cumin, garlic powder and pepper (no Tajín yet). Rest 10–15 min.

Cook: grill on medium-high 8–10 min, turning every 2–3 min, or air fry at 200°C for 12–15 min, shaking halfway, or oven at 220°C fan for 20–25 min, flipping halfway. You want blistered, curled, charred edges.
As soon as they come off the heat: a tiny pinch of sugar, then sprinkle about ¾ tsp Tajín per cob and toss gently.
Mix the sauce and taste it (creamy first, citrus second). Too sharp: add 1 tbsp more mayo.
Finish with feta, coriander, a light extra dust of Tajín and a tiny squeeze of lemon. Serve the sauce on the side to keep them crisp.
tips: Using lime instead: 1 tbsp lime juice max + zest of ½ lime (your Tajín already contains lime and salt).
Try a split finish: half with Tajín + cheese only, half lightly brushed with sauce.
Chef upgrades: chipotle in the sauce (see Chipotle Mayo), brown the butter, a drizzle of hot honey.

recipes.title: Braai Tomato & Onion Relish (Boerie Rolls)

items.name: Mrs Ball's Original Chutney
items.gNote: no Mrs Ball's record; apricot jam used (closest generic: fruit-and-sugar based; errs high)

steps: Cook the onions slowly in the butter and oil over medium-low heat, 20–25 min, until deeply golden and sweet.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook about 2 min until slightly darker.
Add both paprikas and cook 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, Worcestershire, chutney, sugar and vinegar. Simmer uncovered 25–35 min, stirring occasionally, until it barely runs off a spoon.
Season generously with salt and pepper.

nutrition.basis: relish only; the roll and boerewors aren't listed

tips: It should be thick enough to sit on the wors without soaking into the roll.
No green pepper or curry powder; you didn't want them.

recipes.title: Burger Cheese Spread (Smashburgers)
recipes.cookTime: No cooking; chill 30 min (1–2 h better)

items.name: whipped cream cheese
items.note: or block cream cheese plus 2 tbsp milk

ingredients.section: Cheese (your pick: Borden natural Colby/Monterey Jack)

steps: Stir the cream cheese until smooth (add 1 tbsp milk/cream if stiff).
Mix in the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, pepper and salt (if using).
Add the chopped cheese and mix thoroughly.
Refrigerate 30 min minimum (1–2 h better).
Toast the buns, spread 1–2 tbsp on the bun, and put the hot smashed patty straight on. Wait 20–30 sec, then close. Cover briefly for 15–20 sec for an extra melt.
tips: Other cheese options: A) 120–150 g chopped American/processed burger slices (closest smashburger melt). B) 100 g Monterey/Colby Jack + 30–50 g mild cheddar + 20–30 g sharp cheddar. C) Cheddar only: 120 g mild + 30–50 g sharp + 2–4 processed slices.
Sharp cheddar as the main cheese gets greasy/grainy; keep it a minor part.
Block cream cheese: soften 15–20 min (or microwave in 10-sec bursts) and add 2 tbsp milk/cream.
Variations: ½ tsp cayenne or 1–2 tsp jalapeño brine; 1 tbsp pickle juice + ½ tsp mustard powder; ½ tsp extra smoked paprika.
Keeps 5–7 days in the fridge, airtight. Not over 2 h at room temperature. Don't freeze.

recipes.title: Caramelised Onions for Boerie Rolls

items.name: fresh white rolls
items.note: lightly toasted, thin smear of butter

items.name: Mrs Ball's chutney, Dijon/wholegrain mustard, grated mature cheddar

steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add the onions and salt and toss to coat.
Cook slowly 10–15 min, stirring every few minutes, until soft and translucent.
Reduce to low and cook another 25–35 min, stirring every 5–10 min, until deep golden brown. If they stick, add 1 tbsp water (not more oil).
Optional: stir in the brown sugar for 2–3 min, then the balsamic for 2–3 min until glazed.
Season with black pepper and taste for salt.

nutrition.basis: onions only; the rolls, boerewors and sides have no amounts

tips: The preferred "traditional braai" version is just onions, butter, oil, salt and pepper with plenty of time: no sugar, balsamic, garlic or herbs.
Roll: lightly toasted white roll, thin smear of butter, boerewors, onions. Put out chutney, mustard and cheddar so guests can add their own.

recipes.title: Chipotle Mayo

items.name: chipotle powder
items.gNote: no chipotle record; chili powder used

items.name: garlic
items.note: finely grated, or ½ tsp garlic powder

items.name: cumin
items.note: or a few drops Worcestershire, for depth

steps: Mix the mayo and sour cream until smooth.
Add the chipotle powder gradually, tasting as you go.
Add the garlic, lemon/lime and your depth ingredient (cumin or Worcestershire).
Season with salt and pepper. Rest 10–15 min so the powder hydrates.
tips: Too spicy: more mayo/sour cream. Flat: more citrus. Sharp: a little honey. Thick: a splash of water.
Kids' version: ¼ tsp chipotle, a bit more sour cream and a drizzle of honey.
If you do have smoked paprika, add ½ tsp.

recipes.title: KFC-Style Gravy (1 Cup)

items.name: hot water
items.gNote: water (stock adds about 9 kcal a serving)

steps: Dissolve the bouillon in the hot water.
Over medium-low heat, melt the chicken fat/oil with ½ tbsp butter. Whisk in the flour.
Cook, whisking often, until medium brown like milky coffee, about 8–12 min. Don't burn it; this is where the flavour comes from.
Whisk in the onion powder, black and white pepper.
Slowly whisk in the hot bouillon liquid until smooth. Simmer gently about 2 min.
Whisk in the cornflour slurry and simmer 30–60 sec until glossy.
Off the heat, whisk in the remaining ½ tbsp butter, then the sugar, dark soy and MSG.
Taste before adding any salt.
tips: Too thick: a splash of hot water. Too thin: simmer longer or add a bit more slurry. Lumpy: strain or blend.
Double everything for 2 cups.
Only one kind of cube? Use that one, but chicken + beef together tastes best.

recipes.title: NY-Style Pizza Sauce (No-Cook)
steps: Mix everything together. Don't cook it.
Use it lightly; too much sauce makes the pizza soft and wet.
tips: Use grated low-moisture mozzarella. Fresh mozzarella makes it watery unless it's very well drained.

recipes.title: Steakhouse Peppercorn Sauce

items.name: black peppercorns
items.note: coarsely cracked (1 tbsp if not using green peppercorns)

items.name: dried green peppercorns
items.note: rehydrated in hot water 10–15 min; half crushed (or ½ tsp green in brine)
items.gNote: no green-peppercorn record; black pepper used

items.name: brandy or cognac
items.gNote: 55 ml; 80-proof spirit record, counted in full though most alcohol cooks off (errs high; alcohol kcal aren't in P/C/F)

steps: Cook the steaks, remove and rest them. Don't clean the pan; pour off excess fat, leaving 1–2 tsp.
Soak the dried green peppercorns in hot water 10–15 min, drain, and lightly crush half. Coarsely crush the black peppercorns.
Over medium-low heat, cook the shallot and black pepper 1–2 min until the shallot softens without browning.
Add the brandy and bubble 45–60 seconds, scraping up the fond, until only a little liquid remains (no need to flambé).
Add the stock and simmer briskly 3–5 min until reduced by about half and slightly syrupy at the edges.
Lower the heat and stir in the Dijon, Worcestershire and green peppercorns.
Add the cream and simmer gently 3–5 min until it lightly coats a spoon.
Off the heat, swirl in the cold butter. Taste, then add salt only if needed.
tips: The key ratio: reduce 150 ml stock by half, then add 120 ml cream.
No flour or cornflour, and no soy/Marmite needed.
Too thick: add 1–2 tbsp stock or water. Too thin: simmer another minute or two.

Make-ahead for guests: stop slightly thinner than ideal, leave out the butter, cool quickly and refrigerate. Reheat gently, loosen with stock, deglaze the steak pan with 1–2 tbsp sauce and add it back, then finish with the butter.
If it's bitter: add 30–50 ml cream, ½ tsp Dijon and about ⅛ tsp sugar, or 20–30 ml stock. Don't add more pepper or reduce it further.

recipes.title: Tzatziki
recipes.cookTime: No cooking; chill 1 h minimum (ideal 3–4 h)

items.name: cucumber
items.gNote: 400 g peeled, about 150 g water squeezed out (assumed)

steps: Grate the cucumber coarsely, toss with ¼ tsp salt and leave 10–15 min.
Squeeze hard in a towel until very dry.
Let the garlic sit in the vinegar/lemon for 5 min to mellow it.
Mix the yoghurt, garlic, acid, olive oil and salt until completely smooth.
Fold in the cucumber and dill. Taste: needs brightness, a few drops of lemon; too sharp, a little oil; flat, a pinch of salt.
Chill at least 1 h, ideally 3–4 h.
Serve spread in a shallow bowl with a swirl, olive oil and a little dill.
tips: Too loose = thin yoghurt or under-squeezed cucumber. Too thick: add 1–2 tsp cold water or oil, not lemon.
Don't use parsley or low-fat yoghurt.
Serve with grilled lamb, chicken gyros, warm flatbread or roast potatoes.

recipes.title: Baked Vanilla Custard (Crème Brûlée-Style)
recipes.cookTime: 30–40 min at 160°C + 1 h cooling + 4 h (ideally overnight) chilling

items.name: vanilla pod
items.gNote: no vanilla-pod record; 2 tsp extract (the listed swap) used

steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Put 6 ramekins in a deep roasting tray and boil the kettle.
Warm the milk, cream, vanilla pod/seeds and salt over medium-low until steaming; don't boil. Take off the heat, cover and infuse 20–30 min. (If using extract, add it after heating.)
Whisk the yolks and sugar only until smooth and slightly lighter; don't make foam.
Temper: pour a little warm dairy into the yolks while whisking, then gradually add the rest.
Strain through a fine sieve into a jug. Stand 2–3 min and skim off the foam.
Divide between the ramekins. Pour hot water into the tray to halfway up the sides.
Bake 30–40 min, checking from 30. Ready when the edges are set and the centre wobbles like soft jelly.
Remove from the water bath, cool 1 hour at room temperature, then chill at least 4 hours (preferably overnight).
Optional: sprinkle 1–2 tsp white sugar over each cold custard and torch until golden and glassy. Serve straight away.
tips: Gentle heat and not overbaking are what matter most. If it looks fully set in the oven, it may turn grainy.
Use white sugar for the brûlée; brown sugar burns patchily.
Make 1–3 days ahead, covered in the fridge. Torch just before serving.
Serve plain with nutmeg, or with berries, poached fruit, caramel sauce or shortbread.

recipes.title: Fluffy Pancakes (Eden-Style, Double Batch)

items.name: almond milk
items.note: or milk; plus a little extra if needed

steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl whisk the eggs, Greek yogurt, almond milk and oil until reasonably smooth.
Pour the wet into the dry and fold gently until just combined. A few small lumps are good; don't overmix.
Rest the batter 5–10 minutes. It should be thick, soft and spoonable, not pourable.
Heat a non-stick pan over low-medium to medium heat and grease lightly.
Spoon in medium pancakes and keep them fairly thick.
Cook 2–3 min until bubbles appear, the edges set and the underside is golden.
Flip once and cook 1–2 min more until cooked through. Serve immediately.

extra.name: oil for greasing the pan
extra.note: step 5; amount not given, 2 tsp assumed

tips: Too thick? Add almond milk 1 tbsp (15 ml) at a time. Don't add more yogurt; it makes them heavy and gummy.
Don't rest the batter overnight. The raising agents lose their lift. 20–30 min in the fridge is the maximum.
A lid helps thick pancakes cook through. If they brown too fast, lower the heat.
Single batch (6–8 pancakes): halve everything (160 g flour, 7 g baking powder, 1.75 g soda, 33 g sugar, 3/8 tsp salt, 2 eggs, 135 g yogurt, 67 g milk, 25 g oil, optional 1 tsp vanilla).

recipes.title: Play Dough (No-Cook, Metric)
steps: Mix the flour, salt and cream of tartar in a large bowl.
Add the oil, colouring and glycerine.
Add boiling water gradually, starting with about 250–260 ml. Mix with a spoon first because it's hot.
Once cool enough, knead by hand 3–5 min.
Add more boiling water only if it's dry or crumbly; knead in a little flour if it's sticky.
tips: Don't leave out the cream of tartar; it gives stretch and smoothness.
Not edible (very high salt). Supervise young children.
